headline: Network-based simulations model pathogen spread across human, crop, and mosquito systems
label: Network Structured Transmission Modeling
summary: Individual-based network models now address respiratory outbreaks, soybean leaf spot, and gene drive malaria control using explicit structure and simulation at…
synthesis: The shared thread is explicit structure in transmission: each item models spread through a network or spatial framework. A preprint uses large-scale actor-based simulation on dynamic contact networks built from Dutch registry data to assess interventions against early respiratory pathogen spread. A second preprint applies network-based modeling to Frogeye Leaf Spot, caused by Cercospora sojina, in soybean, where yield losses reach 30-60%. A published study pairs a deep learning surrogate with individual-based simulations of CRISPR suppression gene drive mosquitoes, mapping parameters to Anopheles suppression and malaria outcomes in a spatially explicit setting. What is new across these is the combination of structured representation with simulation at scale, and in the malaria work, surrogate modeling that makes parameter mapping tractable. Host systems and scales differ, so the common thread is methodological rather than biological.
